background: Lloyds Banking Group is the holding company of the UK's largest retail and commercial bank, owner of Lloyds Bank, Halifax, Bank of Scotland and Scottish Widows, with almost all of its business in Britain.
synthesis: As a holding company its ratings sit below the banks': A on average across two of the three main agencies, the weakest of them at A-, both on a stable outlook, with a one-notch upgrade by one of the three on 10 Sep 2025 the latest move. Consolidated capital is mixed against UK majors: CET1 of 13.6% is a little under the peer median, while leverage of 5.1% is in the top quarter. Liquidity is also mixed, with LCR of 144% level with the median and NSFR of 123% below the peer median; leverage has fallen 0.3 points since 30 Jun 2025 and the rest has been flat. The newest flagged item, on 18 Sep 2026, is an online banking outage, and the older items concern the Arena Television fraud lawsuits, an operational and legal matter rather than a solvency one.
